public_rationale: The records support Crusoe's lack of experience at Abilene's scale and repeated OpenAI launch-related capacity surprises. Oracle's September 2024 capacity statement is consistent with the scale assertion, but does not settle its prior record through May 2025 on a comparable basis. Crusoe's earlier cloud activity also limits the broadest reading of “never done this.” The complete three-part claim remains unresolved; missing proof is not contradiction.
limitations: Several relevant contemporary reports could not be read with read_page.
Campus power, computing scale and individual building size are not interchangeable.
The demand evidence relies on news reports reproducing executive statements.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Oracle is building Stargate at a scale it has never built at before, using a partner, Crusoe, that has never done this, for OpenAI, which regularly underestimates the demands it puts on its servers.

statement.excerpt: In simpler terms, you have a company (Oracle) building something at a scale it’s never built at before, using a partner (Crusoe) which has never done this, for a company (OpenAI) that regularly underestimates the demands it puts on its servers.

from_speaker: at a scale it’s never built at before
regularly underestimates the demands it puts on its servers
our_interpretation: The claim contains three assertions, all of which must be established for full support.
Scale means a comparable single-campus AI infrastructure build, assessed primarily by power capacity and computing deployment.
Never done this means Crusoe had not previously delivered a comparable hyperscale campus. It does not mean Crusoe had no computing infrastructure experience.
Regularly underestimates means repeated demand surprises producing capacity shortfalls, rather than outages of any cause.
Never and before refer to the companies' histories through May 27, 2025. The historical window therefore has no specified starting date.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable project records establish unprecedented scale for Oracle and no prior comparable delivery by Crusoe, while repeated documented demand surprises establish the OpenAI component.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable prior projects refute either experience assertion, or demand-planning evidence refutes the asserted recurring underestimation. If other components are established, the combined result is mixed.

evidence.explanation: The paragraph reports that Crusoe's leadership acknowledged having no experience building anything close to Abilene's scale. This supports the comparable-campus reading of the Crusoe component.

evidence.locator: Altman quotation in the paragraph discussing GPT-4.5
evidence.explanation: The report connects GPT-4.5's restricted launch to a growth-related GPU shortfall and describes another capacity-limited image-generation launch in March. This supports repeated demand surprises, although it is not a complete demand-forecast record.

Oracle's reported maximum in September 2024 is consistent with Abilene representing a larger undertaking. The statement includes facilities under construction and does not establish the complete comparison at the May 2025 cutoff.

Crusoe had prior cloud infrastructure activity and announced GPU colocation with atNorth. This cautions against treating the claim as absence of all relevant experience, but does not establish prior delivery of a comparable campus.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A comparable inventory or explicit company statement establishing Oracle's largest previously delivered campus as of May 27, 2025, together with clearer records distinguishing the participants' construction roles.
